findings.title: RSS feed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method: raw_html, which makes Post#cook return raw unchanged (app/models/post.rb line 133). When called from the PollFeed path (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb line 35-36), `contents` is the raw feed item content with only CGI.unescapeHTML applied — no HTML sanitization occurs. The embed view (app/views/embed/best.html.erb line 19) then renders these posts with `raw post.cooked`. Any <script>, inline event handlers, or other malicious markup in the external feed is stored verbatim and executed in the Discourse origin for every visitor of the embedded page, allowing a compromised or malicious feed to hijack Discourse sessions/perform CSRF. The import_remote path limits tags/attributes via readability, but the feed path has no such filtering; contents should be sanitized (e.g. via Sanitize/Nokogiri whitelist) before being stored as raw_html.

findings.title: Referer header injected unescaped into inline JavaScript
findings.body: The layout embeds `'<%= request.referer %>'` directly inside a <script> block. The referer is an attacker-controlled HTTP header; ensure_embeddable only checks that URI(referer).host equals the configured embeddable_host, so a referer such as `http://<embeddable_host>/';alert(1);//` passes the host check and breaks out of the JS string literal (and `</script>` sequences break out of the script tag entirely), executing arbitrary script in the Discourse iframe origin. The value must be JSON/JS-escaped (e.g. `json_escape`/to_json) and ideally validated as a full origin before interpolation.

findings.title: PollFeed crashes on feed items without content
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` calls methods on i.content without checking presence. Many RSS feeds provide only a description/summary and no content element (simple-rss returns nil for missing tags), so the scheduled job will raise NoMethodError on nil. With `sidekiq_options retry: false` the exception is swallowed and, more importantly, it aborts processing of the remaining feed items in the same run, so topics after the offending item are never imported until the next hour. Guard with `i.content || i.description` or a nil check.

findings.title: feed_key is dead code; no conditional-fetch deduplication is implemented
findings.body: The `feed_key` method (used nowhere) and its 'feed-modified:' redis key suggest the intent was to skip polling when the feed has not changed (e.g. via Last-Modified/ETag), but poll_feed unconditionally re-opens the feed URL and re-processes every item every hour. Every existing embed's content is re-fetched/recomputed and each unchanged item still goes through a TopicEmbed lookup and SHA1 comparison; if content SHA matches it is skipped only after the DB read. Either remove the dead method or wire it up to store/compare the feed's modified time so polling is skipped when unchanged.

findings.title: Weak origin check on postMessage via substring match
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any message whose origin appears anywhere in discourseUrl. E.g. with discourseUrl 'http://meta.discourse.org', a sender at 'http://meta.discourse.org.evil.com' passes the check (its origin string contains the discourseUrl as a substring) and can drive iframe.height with arbitrary values. The check should compare the parsed origin of discourseUrl to e.origin with strict equality.

findings.title: setnx followed by separate expire is not atomic
findings.body: retrieved_recently? uses $redis.setnx and then a separate $redis.expire. If the process dies (or redis restarts) between the two calls, the key 'retrieved:<url>' exists with no TTL and permanently blocks retrieval for that embed URL until manual redis intervention. Use a single SET key value EX 60 NX (or setex-style) operation so the TTL is set atomically with the key creation.

findings.title: Update path crashes if the embedded post has been deleted
findings.body: On re-import of an existing embed, `post = embed.post` is used without a nil check before `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `embed.update_column`. If the topic's post was deleted (or post_id points to a removed record — the association has no dependent handling and nothing destroys the TopicEmbed when its post is destroyed), the poll job will raise NoMethodError on nil every run for that URL. Guard for a missing post (and consider destroying the TopicEmbed alongside the post).
